summary: New pinned patch set memory-retrieval-warm in the existing openclaw-compat owner: the memory-core recall WorkerTaskPool keeps its worker 30 min (idleTimeoutMs 18e5) instead of the 60 s default. Applied by runtime-sync (Gateway restart on applied) and gateway-start, checked every 30 min, undone by companion-deploy rollback.
reason: S24 31/10, OpenClaw 2026.9.6: brain turns spend 3.6-11 s in Gateway preparation, 0.17 s of it in the Samantha plugin. Inspector NodeWorker shows the Gateway starting memory-search.worker.js right after the tool catalogue on a turn after a pause; the recall pool has no idleTimeoutMs, so WorkerTaskPool retires it after 60 s and nearly every spoken turn pays the respawn (~2.5 s on 4 cores) before the model starts. Read probes (chat.history, sessions.list) do not warm it; OpenClaw 2026.10.9 does not change it.

capabilities.reason: OpenClaw worker pool option through the existing compatibility owner; no route, action or capability.

architecture.reason: Fifth patch set of the existing pinned owner; no new store, scheduler or daemon. The worker pool keeps its own memory-critical retirement (timeout above zero).

evidence: Gateway worker pool lifetime only; MCP tools and schemas unchanged.

limitations: The expected gain (~2 s on a turn after a pause) is inferred from timings and worker spawn offsets; it is confirmed only by the before/after measurement on the S24 after deployment.
The kept worker costs resident memory on a phone with little free RAM; measured after deployment, retired by the pool on memory-critical pressure.
The sqlite-store.worker respawn (~2.2 s SQLite queue wait) is not addressed here.
rollback: companion-deploy.sh of the previous commit undoes the set (manifest not owned by the previous checkout), or whatsapp-network-recovery.py --patch-set memory-retrieval-warm --rollback then a Gateway restart.
